spec.name: Job Posting Analyzer
spec.description: Parses a raw job posting into a structured summary with skills, salary, remote policy, red flags, and an attractiveness score for a senior engineer.

posting_text.description: Raw text of the job posting (may include title, description, requirements, benefits, salary info).

candidate_profile.description: Optional short description of the evaluating candidate's background to tailor the attractiveness score (defaults to a generic senior software engineer).

nodes.name: Normalize posting text
nodes.description: Strip HTML tags and boilerplate, collapse whitespace, and detect if the text is too short/garbled to analyze.

nodes.name: Extract structured fields
nodes.description: Extract title, seniority, skills split, salary, remote policy, and red flags with verbatim evidence from the normalized posting.

config.system: You are a meticulous job-posting analyst. Use ONLY the information present in the posting text — never invent salary figures, skills, or quotes. Do not infer protected-class or demographic information. Output only what the schema requires.
config.prompt:
Analyze this job posting text:

{{nodes.normalize.output.text}}

Rules:
- seniority: infer from title keywords AND years-of-experience requirements; use "unknown" if signals conflict or are absent.
- must_have_skills vs nice_to_have_skills: split by cue words ('required', 'must' vs 'preferred', 'plus', 'nice to have'); default to must-have when ambiguous. Short skill strings only (e.g. "Go", "Kubernetes"), never full sentences. Lists must be disjoint.
- salary_range: report ONLY figures stated in the text (min, max, currency, period). Default currency to USD when a $ symbol or US location is present but no currency is stated. Use null if no concrete pay figure appears. If the posting says 'competitive salary' or similar without figures, add a red flag for vague pay.
- remote_policy: one of remote | hybrid | onsite | unclear, based on explicit statements and location requirements.
- red_flags: scan for unrealistic requirement stacks (e.g. 10+ years for a mid role, 5+ unrelated specializations), vague or missing pay, toxic phrasing ('rockstar', 'work hard play hard', 'wear many hats', 'ninja'), unpaid overtime hints, 24/7 or weekend on-call without compensation, and bait-and-switch signals (e.g. entry level but demanding years of experience). EVERY red flag must include 'evidence' as a verbatim or near-verbatim quote from the posting, and a severity of low, medium, or high.
- If the text is too short or garbled to analyze (too_short = {{nodes.normalize.output.too_short}}), return 'unknown' values, empty skill lists, salary_range null, and one red flag noting insufficient information.

Return a single JSON object matching the schema, no extra prose.

nodes.name: Score attractiveness
nodes.description: Compute a 1-10 attractiveness score and one-paragraph rationale for the candidate profile, weighted on skills fit, salary transparency, remote policy, and red-flag severity.

config.system: You are a pragmatic career advisor assessing job postings for a candidate. Be honest and calibrated; do not inflate scores. Base your assessment only on the provided extraction and posting content.
config.prompt:
Candidate profile: {{input.candidate_profile ?? 'generic senior software engineer'}}

Extracted posting analysis:
{{nodes.extract.output | json}}

Compute:
- attractiveness_score: an integer 1-10 (10 = exceptional fit, 1 = strong avoid), weighted on skills fit vs the candidate profile, salary transparency, remote policy, and red-flag severity (high-severity red flags should pull the score down substantially).
- score_rationale: one paragraph that cites at least one specific positive factor and at least one specific negative factor drawn from the posting/extraction.

Return only the JSON object.

nodes.name: Assemble structured summary
nodes.description: Combine extraction and scoring into the final structured_summary object with the score clamped to an integer 1-10.

input.candidate_profile: Senior backend engineer, 8 years Go/Kubernetes, prefers remote.

input.candidate_profile: Staff-level distributed systems engineer, based in Denver, prefers fully remote.

criteria: salary_range is null exactly because no concrete pay figure appears in the posting.
remote_policy is 'hybrid', consistent with the 'Hybrid (3 days/week, Austin TX)' language.

tests.name: tricky_adversarial_rockstar_posting

input.posting_text: Rockstar Full-Stack Ninja needed! Must know React, Angular, Vue, Node, Python, Java, Kotlin, Swift, AWS, Azure, GCP. 2 years experience. Competitive salary. Work hard play hard! On-site 6 days/week in downtown SF. We're a family! No whiners. This role may also involve occasional janitorial duties.

criteria: salary_range is null because 'competitive salary' contains no concrete figures, and a red flag is present citing the 'competitive salary' language.
remote_policy is 'onsite', consistent with 'On-site 6 days/week in downtown SF'.

Red flags capture at least two of: unrealistic skill breadth vs 2 years experience, 'competitive salary' with no figures, 6-day on-site week, 'family'/'no whiners' culture language, or janitorial duties.
attractiveness_score is a low integer (1-5) and score_rationale references specific negative factors from the posting.

taskSpec.summary: Parses a raw job posting into a structured summary with skills, salary, remote policy, red flags, and an attractiveness score for a senior engineer.
taskSpec.goal: Turn unstructured job posting text into a consistent, structured assessment that a senior engineer can use to quickly decide whether to apply.

inputs.name: posting_text
inputs.description: Raw text of the job posting (may include title, description, requirements, benefits, salary info).
inputs.example: Senior Backend Engineer - We're looking for a rockstar ninja with 10+ years of Go, Kubernetes, and React... Competitive salary. Must be available on-call 24/7.

inputs.name: candidate_profile
inputs.description: Optional short description of the evaluating candidate's background to tailor the attractiveness score (defaults to a generic senior software engineer).
inputs.example: Senior backend engineer, 8 years Go/Kubernetes, prefers remote, dislikes on-call.

outputs.name: structured_summary
outputs.description: Object with fields: title (string), seniority (string: junior|mid|senior|staff|principal|unknown), must_have_skills (array of strings), nice_to_have_skills (array of strings), salary_range (object with min, max, currency, period, or null if not mentioned), remote_policy (string: remote|hybrid|onsite|unclear), red_flags (array of {flag, evidence, severity: low|medium|high}), attractiveness_score (integer 1-10), score_rationale (string).

steps: Normalize the raw posting text (strip HTML/boilerplate, collapse whitespace).
Extract the job title and infer seniority level from title and description language.
Split listed requirements into must-have vs nice-to-have skills using cue words ('required', 'must' vs 'preferred', 'plus', 'nice to have'); default to must-have when ambiguous.
Detect salary information (ranges, single figures, equity/bonus mentions); record null with a red flag if pay is vague or absent while the posting claims 'competitive salary'.
Classify remote policy as remote, hybrid, onsite, or unclear based on explicit statements and location requirements.

Scan for red flags: unrealistic requirement stacks (e.g., 10+ years for a mid role, 5+ unrelated specializations), vague or missing pay, toxic phrasing ('rockstar', 'work hard play hard', 'wear many hats', unpaid overtime hints, 24/7 on-call without compensation), and bait-and-switch signals.
Compute a 1-10 attractiveness score for the candidate profile (default: generic senior engineer), weighting skills fit, salary transparency, remote policy, and red-flag severity.
Emit the structured_summary object with a one-paragraph score rationale citing the strongest positive and negative factors.
constraints: Never invent salary figures; only report what the text states, using null otherwise.
Every red flag must include a verbatim or near-verbatim quote from the posting as evidence.
attractiveness_score must be an integer 1-10; 10 = exceptional fit, 1 = strong avoid.
If the posting text is too short or garbled to analyze, return the structure with 'unknown' values and a red flag noting insufficient information rather than failing.
Do not infer protected-class or demographic information; assess the posting content only.
Output must be a single JSON object matching the declared schema, no extra prose.
successCriteria: Output is valid JSON with all declared fields present (title, seniority, must_have_skills, nice_to_have_skills, salary_range, remote_policy, red_flags, attractiveness_score, score_rationale).
Every red flag entry contains non-empty 'flag', 'evidence', and 'severity' fields, and evidence text appears in (or is a close paraphrase of) the input posting.
salary_range is null exactly when no concrete pay figure appears in the posting; if 'competitive salary' appears without figures, a red flag is present.
remote_policy is one of the four allowed values and is consistent with location/on-site language in the posting.
attractiveness_score is an integer between 1 and 10, and score_rationale references at least one specific positive and one specific negative factor from the posting.
must_have and nice_to_have skills are disjoint lists of short skill strings (no full sentences).
assumptions: Default evaluation persona is a generic senior software engineer when candidate_profile is omitted.
Salary figures default to USD when a currency is not stated but a $ symbol or US location is present.
Seniority is inferred from both title keywords and years-of-experience requirements; 'unknown' is acceptable when signals conflict.
No web lookup is performed; analysis is based solely on provided text.
One posting per invocation; batch processing is out of scope.

exampleInputs.posting_text: Senior Backend Engineer (Remote, US). We need 5+ years with Go and Kubernetes to build our payments platform. Salary: $180k-$220k + equity. Flexible hours, async-first culture. Nice to have: Terraform, AWS.
exampleInputs.candidate_profile: Senior backend engineer, 8 years Go/Kubernetes, prefers remote.

exampleInputs.posting_text: Rockstar Full-Stack Ninja needed! Must know React, Angular, Vue, Node, Python, Java, Kotlin, Swift, AWS, Azure, GCP. 2 years experience. Competitive salary. Work hard play hard! On-site 6 days/week in downtown SF.

Staff Engineer, Platform. Hybrid (3 days/week, Austin TX). Lead our observability team. 8+ years distributed systems, deep Kubernetes expertise required. Compensation: $210,000 base + 15% bonus. Great 401k match.
Junior-ish Developer (we'll train you!) - entry level but must have 7 years commercial React experience. Pay: DOE. Must be available weekends. Fast-paced environment, wear many hats!

plan.rationale: Fixed deterministic sequence: clean text → structured extraction (skills/salary/remote/red flags) → scoring with rationale → assemble final object. No branching, lists, web, or human steps needed; llm_structured guarantees schema-valid fields and code handles normalization exactly.

steps.purpose: Strip HTML tags/boilerplate and collapse whitespace from {{input.posting_text}}; also detect if the text is too short/garbled (< ~40 chars) to analyze.

Extract from the normalized text: title, seniority (junior|mid|senior|staff|principal|unknown), must_have_skills vs nice_to_have_skills split by cue words (default must-have when ambiguous), salary_range (min/max/currency/period or null — never invented, flag 'competitive salary' with no figures), remote_policy (remote|hybrid|onsite|unclear), and red_flags array of {flag, evidence (verbatim quote), severity (low|medium|high)} covering unrealistic stacks, vague pay, toxic phrasing, on-call without compensation, bait-and-switch. If text is too short, return unknown values plus an insufficient-information red flag.

Compute attractiveness_score (integer 1-10) and score_rationale (one paragraph citing at least one specific positive and one specific negative factor), weighted on skills fit vs the candidate profile ({{input.candidate_profile ?? 'generic senior software engineer'}}), salary transparency, remote policy, and red-flag severity.
Combine extract and score outputs into the single structured_summary object with all nine declared fields; clamp attractiveness_score to integer 1-10.

plan.output: structured_summary: object from assemble — title, seniority, must_have_skills, nice_to_have_skills, salary_range (or null), remote_policy, red_flags from extract; attractiveness_score and score_rationale from score.

evolution.change: Change node `assemble` from type `transform` to type `code`.; Replace its config with JavaScript that reads nodes.extract.output and nodes.score.output directly (no string templates), clamps attractiveness_score via Math.round/Math.min/Math.max to an integer 1-10, and returns { structured_summary: ... }.; Keep the declared schema so downstream `output` can still reference {{nodes.assemble.output.structured_summary}}; update the node description.

Replaced the `assemble` transform node with a `code` node that assembles the structured_summary in JavaScript.; The code node explicitly coerces the score with Number(), rounds with Math.round, and clamps to [1, 10] so attractiveness_score is always a genuine integer.; Also defensively defaults skill/red-flag lists to empty arrays and salary_range to null so the assembled object always satisfies the required fields.; Declared the same JSON schema on the code node so the downstream output node can still reference `nodes.assemble.output.structured_summary` as a typed field.; No changes to edges, prompts, or tests were needed — the graph topology and data references remain valid.

No web lookup is performed; analysis is based solely on provided text.
One posting per invocation; batch processing is out of scope.

plan.rationale: Fixed deterministic sequence: clean text → structured extraction (skills/salary/remote/red flags) → scoring with rationale → assemble final object. No branching, lists, web, or human steps needed; llm_structured guarantees schema-valid fields and code handles normalization exactly.

steps.purpose: Strip HTML tags/boilerplate and collapse whitespace from {{input.posting_text}}; also detect if the text is too short/garbled (< ~40 chars) to analyze.

Extract from the normalized text: title, seniority (junior|mid|senior|staff|principal|unknown), must_have_skills vs nice_to_have_skills split by cue words (default must-have when ambiguous), salary_range (min/max/currency/period or null — never invented, flag 'competitive salary' with no figures), remote_policy (remote|hybrid|onsite|unclear), and red_flags array of {flag, evidence (verbatim quote), severity (low|medium|high)} covering unrealistic stacks, vague pay, toxic phrasing, on-call without compensation, bait-and-switch. If text is too short, return unknown values plus an insufficient-information red flag.

Compute attractiveness_score (integer 1-10) and score_rationale (one paragraph citing at least one specific positive and one specific negative factor), weighted on skills fit vs the candidate profile ({{input.candidate_profile ?? 'generic senior software engineer'}}), salary transparency, remote policy, and red-flag severity.
Combine extract and score outputs into the single structured_summary object with all nine declared fields; clamp attractiveness_score to integer 1-10.

plan.output: structured_summary: object from assemble — title, seniority, must_have_skills, nice_to_have_skills, salary_range (or null), remote_policy, red_flags from extract; attractiveness_score and score_rationale from score.
